report: Sagittal CT of the abdomen demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, hypodense mass located in the right upper quadrant, anterior to the liver and displacing adjacent structures. The lesion appears heterogeneous with internal septations or loculations. There is no evidence of calcification within the mass. The visualized spine shows mild degenerative changes.

title: Diagnosis:  64 y.o. female with recurrent breast cancer with metastasis to lymph nodes and lungs.  Liver mass biopsy reveals adenocarcinoma, with histology consistent with breast tissue.
report: There is a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the majority of the right hepatic lobe with areas of lower attenuation. The left hepatic lobe appears compressed and displaced medially by the lesion. No significant pleural effusion or pneumothorax is identified.

title: Intestinal Malrotation
report: The axial CT image demonstrates a large volume of oral contrast within the colon, with multiple loops of bowel containing air and fluid. The coronal reconstruction reveals extensive colonic distension with haustral markings visible throughout the visualized segments. A small amount of residual contrast is noted in the descending colon.

title: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)
report: Axial noncontrast CT of the brain demonstrates diffuse cerebral atrophy with widened sulci and enlarged subarachnoid spaces. There is generalized volume loss of the cerebral hemispheres, resulting in prominent extra-axial CSF spaces. The ventricles appear normal in size without evidence of hydrocephalus.

title: Autosomal Dominant (Adult) Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD)
report: The first image demonstrates bilateral retroperitoneal masses with heterogeneous enhancement and central hypodensities, suggestive of necrosis or cystic change. The second image shows similar findings with more defined renal parenchyma involvement, indicating the masses are likely arising from or involving the kidneys. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis or significant lymphadenopathy in the visualized sections.

title: Cerebellar hemangioblastoma
report: Axial noncontrast CT images of the brain demonstrate a well-circumscribed, hypodense lesion within the right globe, consistent with an intraocular abnormality. The left globe appears unremarkable in comparison. No acute intracranial hemorrhage or midline shift is identified.

title: Cerebellopontine angle meningioma
report: The noncontrast CT demonstrates a large, well-defined lytic lesion involving the left occipital bone with associated soft tissue mass extending into the adjacent subcutaneous tissues. The corresponding T1-weighted MRI shows an isointense to hypointense extra-axial mass in the same region, causing local mass effect on the underlying brain parenchyma without significant edema or midline shift.

title: Bronchial Carcinoid
report: There is a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the right lower hemithorax with associated pleural thickening. The mass appears to be compressing the adjacent lung parenchyma and abutting the diaphragm. No intravenous contrast is present to evaluate for vascular enhancement or mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

title: Sarcoidosis
report: The CT image demonstrates bilateral enlargement of the parotid glands with heterogeneous attenuation. The corresponding coronal T2-weighted MRI shows diffuse hyperintensity within both parotid glands, consistent with increased water content or edema. No discrete mass lesion is identified within the glandular tissue.

title: Pulmonary arteriovenous malformations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
report: The image displays a pulmonary angiogram with contrast opacification of the central pulmonary vasculature. There is a large, radiopaque embolic coil mass located within the right lower lobe pulmonary artery branch. The surrounding lung parenchyma appears clear without evidence of consolidation or pleural effusion.

title: Silent Sinus Syndrome
report: Axial CT images of the head demonstrate bilateral enlargement and sclerosis of the temporal bones with obliteration of the mastoid air cells. The petrous ridges appear thickened, and there is expansion of the squamous portion of the temporal bone bilaterally. No intracranial mass or acute osseous fracture is identified.

title: Intestinal Malrotation
report: Axial CT images of the abdomen demonstrate a large, well-defined hypodense lesion within the right lobe of the liver. The lesion appears to have a thin capsule and is located in the posterior aspect of the right hepatic lobe. No other focal hepatic lesions or significant abnormalities are noted in the visualized portions of the spleen, pancreas, or kidneys.

title: Hepatic adenoma
report: The first image demonstrates a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the left upper quadrant, consistent with splenic enlargement and pathology. The second image shows diffuse hepatosplenomegaly with an enlarged liver and spleen, both exhibiting relatively homogeneous enhancement without focal lesions.

title: HSV Encephalitis
report: The noncontrast CT demonstrates diffuse hyperdensity within the cerebral sulci and basal cisterns, consistent with subarachnoid hemorrhage. The corresponding DWI sequence shows no restricted diffusion in the brain parenchyma.

title: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), right orbital plexiform neurofibroma, sphenoid wing hypoplasia, possible optic nerve glioma.
report: Axial noncontrast CT of the brain demonstrates bilateral proptosis with enlargement of the extraocular muscles. The enlarged muscles appear fusiform in shape, involving the medial, lateral, and inferior recti bilaterally. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect on the suprasellar cisterns.

title: glioblastoma
report: Axial CT of the brain demonstrates a hyperdense, ring-enhancing lesion located in the left parietal lobe. There is associated surrounding hypodensity consistent with vasogenic edema. A subtle rightward midline shift is noted due to the mass effect.

title: Ovarian Cancer metastasis
report: There is a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the majority of the right hemithorax. The left lung demonstrates significant volume loss with associated atelectasis and mediastinal shift to the left. A moderate-sized pleural effusion is present on the right side.

title: Classic Nodular Sclerosing Hodgkin’s Lymphoma (Stage II)
report: The provided images are axial CT scans of the head and neck region, not the chest. The first image demonstrates a hyperdense lesion in the right parapharyngeal space, while the second image shows an enlarged lymph node in the left cervical chain. No pulmonary findings are visible as these are craniofacial studies.

title: CT guided biopsy of liver revealed pt has  cirrhosis with corresponding portal hypertension.  The biopsy of the liver mass was consistent with focal fat deposit, but inconclusive, and will be re-biopsied for definitive diagnosis
report: The first image demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, hypodense mass occupying the right hemithorax with associated compressive atelectasis of the adjacent lung parenchyma. The second image reveals massive hepatomegaly with diffuse enlargement of the liver extending into the left upper quadrant, displacing the stomach and spleen medially.

title: Stage V bilateral Wilms' Tumor
report: Axial CT images of the abdomen demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed, hypodense mass arising from the right kidney. The lesion appears to be exophytic and causes significant mass effect on the adjacent renal parenchyma. A second image at a slightly higher level shows a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the majority of the right hepatic lobe with internal septations or necrotic areas.

title: Microcystic meningioma
report: There is a large, well-circumscribed, hyperdense extra-axial mass located in the right frontal region. The lesion demonstrates homogeneous enhancement and exerts significant mass effect, resulting in compression of the adjacent brain parenchyma and effacement of the ipsilateral lateral ventricle. There is associated midline shift towards the left side.

title: Renal Duplicity (duplication)
report: The noncontrast CT images demonstrate bilateral enlargement of the kidneys with multiple low-attenuation cystic lesions throughout both renal parenchyma. The liver and spleen appear unremarkable in size and attenuation, and no focal hepatic or splenic masses are identified. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis or perinephric stranding.

title: Subependymoma, lateral ventricle
report: Axial noncontrast CT and T1-weighted MRI demonstrate a well-circumscribed, rounded mass lesion centered within the right lateral ventricle. The lesion appears isodense to brain parenchyma on CT and isointense on T1-weighted imaging. There is associated mild dilation of the adjacent right lateral ventricle with no evidence of midline shift or extra-axial extension.

title: Neuroblastoma with intraspinal extension
report: Coronal T2-weighted MRI of the spine demonstrates a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the right renal fossa. The sagittal T2-weighted image reveals a lobulated, hyperintense soft tissue mass located in the retroperitoneum, anterior to the lumbar vertebral bodies and extending into the paraspinal region.

title: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) with optic glioma, dural ectasia, thoracic syrinx.
report: Coronal T1-weighted MRI of the spine demonstrates a well-circumscribed, hyperintense mass located in the left paraspinal region, adjacent to the thoracic vertebral column. The lesion appears extra-axial and does not show evidence of invasion into the spinal canal or vertebral body on this sequence. Sagittal T1-weighted imaging reveals normal alignment of the cervical and thoracic spine with preserved intervertebral disc height and no visible intraspinal mass effect.

title: Radiation Necrosis
report: The T2-weighted image demonstrates a large area of hyperintensity involving the left parietal lobe and extending into the subcortical white matter, consistent with vasogenic edema. This region causes mass effect with effacement of adjacent sulci and compression of the left lateral ventricle. On the post-contrast T1-weighted image, there is a ring-enhancing lesion located in the left parietal lobe, corresponding to the area of abnormality seen on the T2 sequence.

title: Uveal (Choroidal)Melanoma of the left globe with extension of tumor into the retro-ocular tissues
report: Axial T1-weighted MRI images of the orbits demonstrate bilateral enlargement of the extraocular muscles, most prominently involving the inferior recti. The affected muscles appear enlarged and hyperintense relative to surrounding structures without evidence of mass effect or orbital fat stranding.

title: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
report: MR cholangiopancreatography demonstrates a dilated common bile duct containing a hyperintense filling defect. There is associated upstream dilation of the intrahepatic biliary tree and the common hepatic duct.

title: Brain biopsy confirmed patient has glioblastoma multiforme.
report: Axial T2-weighted MRI images of the brain demonstrate multiple ring-enhancing lesions located in the region of the third ventricle and surrounding structures. These lesions exhibit central hypointensity with hyperintense rims, suggestive of cystic or necrotic components surrounded by a capsule-like structure. The lesions appear to be clustered around the midline, involving the hypothalamic-pituitary region and extending into the adjacent brain parenchyma.

title: Lhermitte Duclos disease, Cowden disease
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, hypointense mass occupying the right cerebellar hemisphere with significant mass effect. The corresponding axial T2-weighted image reveals this lesion as markedly hyperintense relative to surrounding brain parenchyma. There is associated compression of the fourth ventricle and effacement of adjacent cisterns due to the space-occupying nature of the lesion.

title: Brain biopsy confirmed glioblastoma multiforme.
report: Axial T2-weighted MRI images demonstrate bilateral periventricular white matter hyperintensities, more pronounced on the left side. There is associated mass effect with effacement of the adjacent sulci and mild compression of the lateral ventricles. No midline shift or hemorrhage is evident.

title: Agenesis of the Corpus Callosum
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates marked dilation of the lateral ventricles with thinning of the overlying cerebral cortex. The axial proton density image confirms severe bilateral ventriculomegaly, particularly involving the occipital horns, consistent with hydrocephalus.

title: Hemangioblastoma (WHO Grade I)
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast MRI images of the brain demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed, hypointense mass located in the right cerebellar hemisphere. The lesion exerts significant mass effect, causing compression and effacement of the fourth ventricle with resultant mild dilation of the supratentorial ventricular system. There is no evidence of hemorrhage or calcification within the lesion on these sequences.

title: Chondrosarcoma of the skull base
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates a well-circumscribed, hyperintense mass located in the nasopharynx. The axial T2-weighted image confirms this finding, showing a corresponding hyperintense lesion within the right nasopharyngeal space. There is no evidence of intracranial extension or significant surrounding edema.

title: Acromegaly from pituitary macroadenoma
report: The images demonstrate a well-circumscribed, round, hypointense lesion located in the region of the sella turcica on the sagittal view. This mass effect is seen compressing the optic chiasm superiorly and displacing the pituitary stalk posteriorly. The coronal view shows an enlarged sellar mass with extension into the suprasellar cistern, causing effacement of the interpeduncular cistern.

title: Alzheimer disease
report: Coronal T1-weighted MRI of the brain demonstrates marked generalized cerebral atrophy with widened sulci and enlarged subarachnoid spaces. There is significant enlargement of the lateral ventricles, consistent with hydrocephalus ex vacuo or communicating hydrocephalus. The basal cisterns appear prominent.

title: Multiple Myeloma
report: There is a large, well-circumscribed extra-axial mass located in the left frontal region. The lesion demonstrates homogeneous signal intensity similar to subcutaneous fat on T1-weighted imaging and causes significant mass effect with compression of the adjacent brain parenchyma. No evidence of intracranial extension or bone destruction is seen.

title: Ependymoma
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates hypointense signal within the vertebral bodies of C2 through C5, with loss of normal marrow signal intensity. The T2-weighted image reveals hyperintense signal in the same region, consistent with edema or fluid accumulation. There is associated collapse and deformity of the affected vertebral bodies, resulting in anterior wedging and kyphotic angulation at the cervicothoracic junction.

title: Spinal meningioma
report: The axial T1-weighted post-contrast image demonstrates a large, heterogeneously enhancing soft tissue mass centered in the posterior mediastinum and extending into the paraspinal region. The sagittal view reveals this mass causing significant anterior displacement of the spinal cord with associated compression. There is no evidence of vertebral body destruction or epidural extension.

title: Maple syrup urine disease
report: Axial T2-weighted MRI images of the brain in a 1-year-old male demonstrate diffuse, symmetric hyperintensity involving the cerebral white matter. The basal ganglia and thalami appear relatively spared compared to the surrounding white matter. There is no evidence of mass effect, midline shift, or hydrocephalus.

title: Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma
report: There is a heterogeneously enhancing mass located in the suprasellar region extending into the sphenoid sinus. The lesion demonstrates irregular borders and appears to be compressing the optic chiasm superiorly. No other focal parenchymal abnormalities are identified.

title: Scheuermann Disease with Kyphosis
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates a large, heterogeneous mass occupying the anterior mediastinum and extending into the retrosternal space. The mass appears hypointense relative to muscle and causes significant mass effect on the adjacent structures. On the corresponding T2-weighted image, the lesion remains largely isointense to slightly hyperintense with internal heterogeneity, without clear evidence of cystic degeneration or fat content. There is no obvious invasion into the vertebral bodies or spinal canal, though the anterior displacement of the heart and great vessels is noted.

title: Budd-Chiari Syndrome
report: There is diffuse enlargement of the liver with heterogeneous signal intensity. The spleen appears enlarged and demonstrates a focal area of high T2 signal within its parenchyma. No ascites or pleural effusion is identified.

title: Alexander  Disease, Rosenthal Fiber Encephalopathy
report: Axial T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI images of the brain in a 1-year-old male demonstrate marked enlargement of the lateral ventricles, consistent with hydrocephalus. The third ventricle is also dilated, and there is associated thinning of the surrounding cerebral parenchyma. No focal mass lesion or midline shift is identified.

title: Neurofibroma
report: Axial T2-weighted image demonstrates a well-circumscribed, hyperintense mass located in the posterior aspect of the thigh musculature. The lesion exhibits high signal intensity relative to surrounding muscle tissue on this sequence. A corresponding hypointense, rounded structure is noted on the adjacent axial T1-weighted noncontrast image.

title: Atrial Septal Defect (ASD).Ostium primum.
report: Axial cardiovascular magnetic resonance images demonstrate a large, well-defined mass within the right atrium. The lesion appears hyperintense on this T2*-weighted sequence and is distinct from the surrounding myocardium. No evidence of pericardial effusion or significant pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities is noted in the visualized sections.

title: Osteochondritis Dissecans Stage IV
report: Coronal T2-weighted MRI of the knee demonstrates a high-signal intensity fluid collection within the intercondylar notch, consistent with an effusion. The posterior cruciate ligament is visualized and appears intact. There is no evidence of significant joint space narrowing or bony erosions.

title: Juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast MRI images of the brain demonstrate a large, heterogeneous mass centered in the posterior fossa. The lesion exhibits mixed signal intensity with areas of hyperintensity and hypointensity, suggestive of solid components and cystic or necrotic changes. There is associated mass effect on the fourth ventricle and compression of the cerebellar hemispheres.

title: Pseudotumor cerebri
report: The coronal T2-weighted image demonstrates bilateral hyperintense signal abnormalities within the cerebellar hemispheres. The sagittal T1-weighted image reveals corresponding hypointense signal changes in the cerebellum, with a 'tiger stripe' or lacy pattern of alternating signal intensity. These findings are localized to the posterior fossa structures.

title: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
report: The T2-weighted image demonstrates hyperintensity within the left frontal lobe, involving both cortical and subcortical regions. The corresponding DWI sequence shows restricted diffusion in the same area, appearing as a bright signal. These findings are localized to the left hemisphere without evidence of midline shift or mass effect.

title: Avascular Necrosis of femoral heads bilaterally with associated osteoarthritic changes.
report: The T2-weighted image demonstrates a hyperintense fluid collection within the bladder and surrounding pelvic structures. The T1-weighted noncontrast image shows corresponding hypointensity in these regions, consistent with fluid signal characteristics. There is no evidence of solid mass or fat-containing lesion within the pelvis.

title: Uterine Leiomyoma
report: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed pelvic mass with heterogeneous signal intensity and internal cystic components. The mass exerts significant mass effect, compressing the urinary bladder anteriorly and displacing bowel loops posteriorly. Axial T2-weighted imaging confirms the presence of this large, complex adnexal or uterine mass occupying the majority of the pelvis.

title: Optic neuritis (NOS)
report: Axial T1-weighted image demonstrates bilateral proptosis with enlargement of the extraocular muscles, particularly involving the medial recti. The axial T2-weighted image confirms symmetric enlargement of the extraocular muscles with intermediate signal intensity and no evidence of intraconal mass or orbital fat stranding.

title: Herpes Encephalitis (HSV 1)
report: Axial T2-weighted MRI images demonstrate a hyperintense lesion in the right frontal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema. The lesion appears to involve both gray and white matter, causing local mass effect on the adjacent lateral ventricle. There is no evidence of midline shift or hydrocephalus. The optic nerves appear intact without abnormal signal.

title: Renal Oncocytoma
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast images demonstrate a large, well-circumscribed, heterogeneous mass arising from the left kidney. The lesion exhibits mixed signal intensity with areas of low and intermediate signal, suggesting internal complexity such as hemorrhage or necrosis. On post-contrast imaging, the mass shows heterogeneous enhancement with peripheral rim enhancement and central hypoenhancing regions. The right kidney appears unremarkable in size and morphology.

title: Meningioma, Falx
report: Axial and sagittal SWI images demonstrate a well-circumscribed, hyperintense lesion within the right globe consistent with an intraocular mass. The lesion exhibits signal voids suggestive of hemorrhage or calcification. No evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or midline shift is observed in the brain parenchyma.

title: Septo-Optic Dysplasia
report: Axial and coronal T2-weighted MRI images of the brain demonstrate marked enlargement of the lateral ventricles with prominent periventricular lucency, consistent with transependymal CSF flow. The third ventricle is also dilated, and there is no evidence of mass effect or midline shift. The cortical sulci appear effaced, suggesting increased intracranial pressure.

title: Bilateral avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral heads
report: Coronal T2-weighted image demonstrates a hyperintense fluid collection within the right hip joint and surrounding soft tissues. The corresponding T1-weighted noncontrast image shows hypointensity in these same regions, consistent with fluid. There is associated marrow signal abnormality within the right proximal femur and acetabulum.

title: Tuberous Sclerosis
report: The T2-weighted image demonstrates diffuse hyperintensity within the subcutaneous tissues and scalp, consistent with extensive soft tissue edema. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect. The T1-weighted post-contrast image shows enhancement of the scalp and subcutaneous tissues, confirming the presence of inflammation or infection in these regions. No abnormal parenchymal signal intensity or contrast enhancement is seen within the brain parenchyma itself.

title:
Autosomal Dominant "Adult" Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD).  

Family Hx revealed PT's father with history of HTN, RF, and subarachnoid hemmorhage.
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast MRI demonstrates bilateral renal enlargement with multiple hypointense cystic structures replacing normal parenchyma. The corresponding T2-weighted image reveals these lesions as markedly hyperintense, consistent with fluid-filled cysts of varying sizes. There is significant distortion of the renal architecture and loss of corticomedullary differentiation bilaterally.

title: Meningioma, WHO Grade 1
report: The axial T2-weighted MRI images demonstrate a large, hyperintense mass lesion in the left frontal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema. There is significant mass effect causing midline shift to the right and compression of the left lateral ventricle. The second image also reveals a smaller area of abnormal signal intensity in the right parietal region.

title: Myxopapillary Ependymomas
report: The image displays a sagittal T1-weighted MRI of the lumbar spine with gadolinium contrast. There is extensive abnormal enhancement involving multiple vertebral bodies, particularly from L2 through S1, which appear hyperintense relative to normal marrow. The intervertebral discs between these levels also demonstrate significant enhancement and loss of normal signal intensity. This pattern suggests an infiltrative process affecting both the bone marrow and disc spaces.

title: Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Heads
report: Coronal T1-weighted images demonstrate bilateral femoral head and neck marrow signal abnormalities with heterogeneous low-to-intermediate signal intensity. Coronal T2-weighted fat-suppressed sequences reveal corresponding hyperintense signal within the affected bone marrow, particularly prominent in the right femoral head and neck region. There is associated soft tissue edema surrounding the right hip joint.

title: Hyperostosis Frontalis Interna
report: The sagittal MRI of the brain demonstrates marked generalized atrophy with widened cortical sulci and enlarged subarachnoid spaces. The ventricular system appears prominent, particularly the third ventricle, consistent with ex-vacuum dilation. There is no evidence of mass effect or midline shift.

title: Parasellar Meningioma and arachnoid cyst
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed extra-axial mass in the posterior fossa causing significant mass effect and compression of the fourth ventricle. The coronal T2-weighted image reveals multiple small, air-filled locules within the mastoid air cells bilaterally, consistent with mastoiditis or aerated mastoid air cells. No intracranial hemorrhage or acute infarction is identified.

title: Plantar Fibromatosis (Ledderhose Disease)
report: The sagittal T1-weighted noncontrast image demonstrates a large, well-defined fluid collection within the plantar aspect of the foot. On the post-contrast fat-suppressed sequence, this lesion shows intense enhancement with internal septations and solid components, indicating vascularity or tissue content.

title: Osteochondritis dissecans.
report: Sagittal MR images of the ankle demonstrate extensive marrow signal abnormality within the talus and calcaneus. There is associated soft tissue edema and fluid tracking along the posterior aspect of the heel. The findings are consistent with significant bone marrow pathology involving the hindfoot.

title: Chondrosarcoma metastatic to Brain
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast images demonstrate a large, multiloculated cystic mass in the left parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema and mild midline shift. A smaller, separate cystic lesion is also noted in the left frontal region. On T2-weighted imaging, these lesions appear hyperintense, consistent with fluid content, and are surrounded by extensive hyperintense signal changes indicative of significant perilesional edema.

title: Cervical Cord hemangioblastoma
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates hypointense signal within the vertebral bodies of C3 through C6. The corresponding T2-weighted image reveals hyperintense signal changes in these same vertebral bodies, consistent with edema or marrow replacement. There is associated loss of normal height and kyphotic deformity at this level.

title:
1. Mid-substance anterior cruciate ligament tear.
2. Lateral capsular avulsion consistent with Segond fracture.
3. Partial thickness tear of medial collateral ligament.
report: The sagittal MRI images of the knee demonstrate a large, heterogeneous mass involving the distal femur and proximal tibia. There is extensive soft tissue extension with high signal intensity on this sequence, suggesting significant fluid or edema component. The normal marrow architecture is replaced by this abnormality, which appears to breach the joint space.

title: Meningioma of planum sphenoidale
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast images demonstrate a large, heterogeneous mass in the right frontal lobe with significant surrounding vasogenic edema and midline shift. Post-contrast T1-weighted imaging reveals intense, irregular enhancement of the lesion with central areas of necrosis or cystic change. The mass exerts substantial mass effect on the adjacent lateral ventricle, causing compression and distortion of the right frontal horn.

title: Myxopapillary ependymoma.
report: Axial MRI images of the lumbar spine demonstrate a large, expansile mass centered within the vertebral body. The lesion exhibits heterogeneous signal intensity with areas of high T2 signal and enhancement on post-contrast T1-weighted imaging. There is associated expansion and thinning of the cortical bone, with extension into the posterior elements and epidural space.

title: Chiari II Malformation
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed extra-axial mass located in the posterior fossa. This lesion causes significant mass effect with compression of the fourth ventricle and upward displacement of the cerebellar vermis. The axial FLAIR sequence confirms the presence of this hyperintense lesion within the posterior fossa, which appears to be compressing the brainstem.

title: Takayasu Arteritis
report: The MRA demonstrates a tortuous and dilated thoracic aorta with an irregular contour. There is significant narrowing of the distal abdominal aorta, suggestive of occlusion or severe stenosis. The iliac arteries appear hypoplastic or absent.

title: Bicuspid Aortic Valve with Aortic Stenosis and Aortic Dilatation.
report: Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large, well-defined, rounded mass arising from the right atrium and extending into the right ventricle. The mass appears hyperintense relative to the myocardium on this sequence, suggesting high water content or slow flow characteristics. There is no evidence of pericardial effusion or significant invasion into adjacent structures.

title: Osteochondritis Dissecans, juvenile-type
report: Coronal T1-weighted MRI of the knee demonstrates a large, well-defined, lobulated mass arising from the proximal tibia. The lesion exhibits mixed signal intensity with areas of low signal consistent with cartilage and intermediate signal suggesting bone or fibrous tissue. There is significant expansion of the tibial metaphysis with thinning of the overlying cortex but no frank cortical breach is visualized.

title: Chiari I Malformation
report: The sagittal T1-weighted MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed extra-axial mass located in the posterior fossa. The lesion exhibits homogeneous isointensity relative to the brain parenchyma and causes significant mass effect with compression of the fourth ventricle and upward displacement of the cerebellar vermis. There is no evidence of internal hemorrhage or cystic change within the mass.

title: Choroid Plexus Papilloma
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates marked atrophy of the cerebellar vermis with widening of the interfolial spaces. There is significant volume loss in the posterior fossa, resulting in an enlarged fourth ventricle and prominent cisterna magna. The axial T1-weighted image confirms severe hypoplasia or aplasia of the cerebellar vermis, with near-complete absence of midline folia.

title: Cerebral Cavernous Malformation
report: Axial T1-weighted noncontrast images demonstrate a hypointense lesion in the right frontal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema. Post-contrast T1-weighted imaging reveals an irregular, heterogeneously enhancing mass within the same region, suggestive of a neoplastic process. There is no evidence of midline shift or hydrocephalus.

title:
Multiple Myeloma
Diagnosis was confirmed by biopsy of humeral lesion and bone marrow aspirate.
report: There is a large, heterogeneously enhancing mass located within the proximal humeral metaphysis and extending into the diaphysis. The lesion demonstrates cortical destruction and expansion of the bone with associated soft tissue extension. No significant joint effusion or dislocation is visualized.

title: Septo-Optic Dysplasia
report: Axial T2-weighted MRI of the brain demonstrates a focal area of abnormal signal intensity within the genu of the corpus callosum. This region exhibits mixed signal characteristics, with areas of both hyperintensity and hypointensity relative to the surrounding normal white matter. The ventricular system appears symmetric without evidence of hydrocephalus or mass effect.

title: Osteochondritis dissecans
report: The coronal T1-weighted image demonstrates a large, well-defined soft tissue mass in the posterior aspect of the ankle/foot region. The sagittal T2-weighted image reveals this lesion as hyperintense with internal heterogeneity and surrounding edema within adjacent muscle groups.

title: PANK 2 (Hallervorden-Spatz) PKAN (Pantothenate Kinase Associated Neurodegeneration)
report: Axial SWI and coronal T2-weighted images demonstrate bilateral symmetric hyperintensities within the globus pallidus. There is also a prominent area of signal abnormality involving the splenium of the corpus callosum. No evidence of hemorrhage or mass effect is seen.

title: Myxopapillary Ependymoma
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates hypointense signal within the spinal cord at the thoracolumbar junction. The corresponding T2-weighted image reveals a hyperintense intramedullary lesion with associated cord expansion and edema. There is no evidence of an enhancing mass or cystic component on these non-contrast sequences.

title: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
report: The first image demonstrates bilateral hyperintense signal within the globes of the eyes on T2-weighted imaging. The second image reveals diffuse cortical and subcortical hyperintensities throughout the cerebral hemispheres, particularly prominent in the occipital regions, with associated sulcal effacement.

title: Intradural Extramedullary Meningioma.
report: Axial FIESTA MRI images of the thoracic spine demonstrate a hyperintense lesion within the spinal cord parenchyma. The lesion is centrally located and appears to cause some expansion of the cord contour. There is no evidence of significant mass effect or compression of the surrounding neural foramina.

title: Medulloblastoma confirmed by pathology.
report: The sagittal T1-weighted image demonstrates marked enlargement of the lateral ventricles with thinning of the corpus callosum. The axial proton density image reveals a large, well-circumscribed, hyperintense mass occupying the fourth ventricle and extending into the cerebellar parenchyma. This lesion causes significant obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow, resulting in severe hydrocephalus.

title: MYXOID LIPOSARCOMA
report: Axial T1-weighted image demonstrates a well-circumscribed, hyperintense lesion within the subcutaneous fat of the anterior thigh musculature. The corresponding axial T2-weighted image reveals this same lesion as markedly hyperintense with smooth margins and no evidence of internal septations or solid components.

title: Avascular necrosis (AVN) of femoral heads bilaterally
report: Coronal T1-weighted MRI images of the pelvis demonstrate a large, heterogeneous mass centered in the left acetabulum and proximal femur. The lesion exhibits mixed signal intensity with areas of low signal consistent with cortical destruction and soft tissue extension into the surrounding musculature. There is associated expansion and remodeling of the bony architecture on the left side compared to the right.

title: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease
report: The coronal T2-weighted image demonstrates a large, well-defined cystic structure in the left upper quadrant with internal septations and fluid-fluid levels. The axial T2-weighted image reveals a similar complex cystic lesion with multiple loculations and high signal intensity on T2, consistent with fluid content. No solid components or restricted diffusion are evident within the lesions.
